notes: Figure-fidelity sweep. This batch turned out to contain essentially no general-format diagrams: the only syntax skeleton on any of these twelve pages is the one-line USING clause general format on p.542 ('USING identifier-1'), whose underline on the required word USING is correctly preserved as <u>USING</u> in the markdown. There are therefore NO choice-indicator (5.2.6.4 vertical bar) sites, no unclosed brackets/braces, and no ellipsis-placement (5.2.7) sites to lose on these pages. All twelve pages were compared line by line against the rendered PDF; the numeric literals in the FLOAT-DECIMAL/FLOAT-BINARY NOTEs on pp.538-539 were digit-counted against zoomed crops and match the printed glyphs exactly (including ISO's own defects, e.g. the 15-digit '-9.999 999 999 999 99E+384' on p.538 and the 34-nine value on p.539). Only two cosmetic transcription artifacts were found.

findings.pdf_says: and each corresponding occurrence of the data item referenced by identifier-2.
findings.markdown_says: and each corresponding occurrence of the data item referenced by identifier-**2**.
findings.why_it_matters: Stray markdown emphasis delimiters were injected around the operand ordinal. The PDF prints plain 'identifier-2' with no emphasis. Read as plain text (which is how the spec is grepped for operand names) the token becomes 'identifier-**2**', so a literal search for 'identifier-2' misses this sentence. It is a known recurring artifact in this transcription (the same pattern appears at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 32469: 'literal-**1**', 'identifier-**2**', 'character positions**.**'), so it should be swept, not fixed in isolation.
findings.suggested_repair: In specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 22821 replace 'identifier-**2**.' with 'identifier-2.', and sweep the file for the sibling pattern /(?:identifier|literal|subscript|index|data-name)-\*\*\d+\*\*/ plus stray '**.**'.

findings.why_it_matters: 'variable-occurrence data item' is a defined ISO term (see 8.5.1.6 / 13.18.38 OCCURS clause). The page-boundary rejoin left a space after the intrinsic hyphen, splitting the defined term into two tokens, so a search of the spec for 'variable-occurrence data item' does not find this General rule 6 of the VALUE clause.
findings.suggested_repair: In specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 23080 replace 'variable- occurrence data item' with 'variable-occurrence data item'; sweep for other '<word>- <word>' page-boundary rejoins of hyphenated defined terms.
